εἰπόντι ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωή, κυριεύων τῶν τοιούτους καρποὺς ἐνηνοχότων. ἐν ᾧ θανάτῳ
οὐκ ἐ τὶν ὁ μνημονεύων θεοῦ· καὶ γὰρ πᾶς ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ τέθνηκεν τῷ θεῷ καὶ ζῇ τῷ
θανάτῳ, ὅπερ ταὐτόν ἐστιν τῷ ζῇν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ. ἡμέτερος καρπὸς εἰς ἁγιασμόν· οὐχ
ἡμέτερος δέ, οὐδὲ κατὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν φύσιν, ὁ φέρων τῷ ἤδη συνησθημένῳ αὐτοῦ
αἰσχύνην. ὅτι δὲ ἡμέτερον μὲν τὸ κρεῖττον, οὐ τοιοῦτον δὲ τὸ χεῖρον, δηλοῖ καὶ ὁ
σωτὴρ λέγων εἰ τὸ ἀλλότριον ἐπι τεύθητε καὶ οὐκ ἐγένε θε ἄξιοι, τὸ ὑμέτερον τί
ὑμῖν δώ ει; κἂν γὰρ μὴ γενώμεθα ἄξιοι τοῦ κρείττονος, ὡς ἡμέτερον αὐτὸ τῇ φύσει
οὐ λαμβάνομεν διὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν. ἐρεῖ δέ τις ἐνταῦθα τὸν εἰς ἁγιασμὸν καρπὸν εἶναι
τῶν δεδου λωμένων τῷ θεῷ τὴν παντελῆ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀφροδισίων καθάρευσιν· καί
φησιν ὁ τοιοῦτος τοῖς μὲν ἐν γάμῳ ἁρμόζειν τὸ ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας
ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, τοῖς δὲ ἐν ἁγνείᾳ ὡς μεῖζον τὸ νυνὶ δὲ ἐλευθερω θέντες
ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· ὥστε τὸν μὲν ἔσχατον καρπὸν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἁγιασμὸν διὰ
τὸ δεδουλῶσθαι τῷ θεῷ δεδουλῶσθαι πολὺ πρότερον τῇ δικαιο σύνῃ μὴ πάντως
ἔχειν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἁγιασμὸν διὰ τὸν κατὰ υγγνώμην λόγον. 34 vi 23 τὰ γὰρ
ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ
τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν. καλὴ ἡ διαφορά, ὀψωνίου μὲν ἐπὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τεταγμένου,
χαρίσματος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ θεοῦ· οὔτε γὰρ ὀψώνια ὡς ὀφειλόμενα δίδωσιν ὁ θεὸς ἀλλὰ
χάρισμα, οὐδὲ χάρισμα ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀλλ' ὀφειλόμενα ὀψώνια. τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ
οὐκ ἔταξεν ἁπλῶς ζωὴ αἰώνιος, ἀτελὴς γὰρ αὕτη νοεῖται ὅτε μὴ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ
ἐστιν τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν. δηλοῦται δὲ ὅτι ἡ ἁμαρτία τῷ βασιλευομένῳ ὑπ' αὐτῆς δίδωσι
τὸν θάνατον, καὶ οὐχ ὁ θεὸς ἐπιφέρει τὸν ἐχθρὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ θάνατον, ὁ γὰρ θεὸ
θάνατον οὐκ ἐποίη εν καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. ἐὰν δέ τις πρὸς τοῦτο ἀνθυποίσῃ καὶ τὸ ἐγὼ
ἀποκτενῶ καὶ ζῇν ποιή ω καὶ κύριο θανατοῖ καὶ ζωογονεῖ, ἐροῦμεν ὅτι ἀποκτέννει ὁ
θεὸς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἵνα μετὰ τοῦτο ζωοποιήσῃ τὸν ἀποθανόντα τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ. 35 vii 1–3 ἢ
ἀγνοεῖτε, ἀδελφοί, γινώσκουσι γὰρ νόμον λαλῶ, ὅτι ὁ νόμος κυριεύει τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
ἐφ' ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ; ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ· ἐὰν δὲ
ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός. ἄρα οὖν ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς
μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα
ἐστὶν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, τοῦ μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν μοιχαλίδα γενομένην ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ. τὸ
γινώσκειν τὸν νόμον πάντως οἶδεν τὴν διαφορὰν τῆς ἐν αὐτῷ παλαιότητο τοῦ
γράμματο καὶ τῆς ἐνυπαρχούσης τοῖς νοήμασιν αὐτοῦ καινότητο τοῦ πνεύματο ·
τοῦτο γάρ ἐστι τὸ τελείως γινώσκειν τὸν νόμον. ἐπιφέρει δὲ καὶ παράδειγμα, σφόδρα
τῷ προκειμένῳ κατάλληλον· ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ·
ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνὴρ κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός· ὁ νόμος ἐστὶν ὁ ἀνήρ·
δῆλον δὲ ὅτι ὁ κατὰ τὸ γράμμα· οὗτος γὰρ καὶ τὸ ἀποθνήσκειν ἐπεδέξατο διὰ τὸ εἶναι
παλαιότη γράμματο · τὸ δὲ παλαιού μενον καὶ γηρά κον ἐγγὺ ἀφανι μοῦ. λέγεται δὲ
καὶ ἀποθνήσκειν καὶ ἐπεὶ μηδὲ παρὰ τοῖς βουλομένοις αὐτὸν φυλάσσειν καὶ οὕτω
προαιρουμένοις, ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω, ζῇ. 36 vii 6 νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου,
ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα, ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ
οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος. τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἀεί ἐστιν ἐν καινότητι, οὔτε
παλαιούμενον οὔτε γηρά κον ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον τοῦ ἔ ω ἡμῶν ἀνθρώπου
ἀνακαινουμένου ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ· καὶ ἡ παλαιότης δὲ τοῦ γράμματος οὐκ ἔστιν ὅτε
καινὴ ἦν, οὐδὲ ὁ παλαιὸ ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπο καινός ποτε ἦν, ὅστις ἅμα τῷ ὑποστῆναι
πεπαλαίωται, οὐ χρόνῳ ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιῶνδε νοημάτων καὶ ἔργων παλαιωσάντων
αὐτόν. vii 7 <τί οὖν; ὁ νόμος ἁμαρτία; οὐχ ὥσπερ ὄνομα ἕν ἐστι νόμος, οὕτω καὶ εἷς ὁ
περὶ νόμου πανταχοῦ τῆς γραφῆς λόγος. διὸ καθ' ἕκαστον χρὴ τόπον αὐτῆς
ἐπιμελῶς ἐπιστήσαντα θεωρῆσαι, νῦν μὲν τί σημαίνεται ἐκ τῆς νόμος φωνῆς, νῦν δὲ
τί χρὴ τὸ τοιοῦτον ἐννοεῖν. ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ἄλλων πλειόνων· ὁμώνυμοι γὰρ καὶ ἐπὶ
ἄλλων εἰσὶ κατὰ τὴν γραφὴν φωναί, αἵτινες συγχέουσι τοὺς νομίζοντας ὅτι ὡς
ὄνομα ἕν ἐστιν οὕτω καὶ τὸ σημαινόμενον ἕν, ὅπου ἂν τοῦτο ὀνομασθῇ. ὅτι δὲ ἡ
νόμος φωνὴ οὐκ ἐπὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἀλλ' ἐπὶ πλειόνων τέτακται, τὰ πολλὰ παραλιπόντες
καὶ δεόμενα κατασκευῆς, ἔχοντα ἀνθυποφορὰν λύσεως δεομένην, ἐκθησόμεθα τὰ
πάνθ' ὁντινοῦν δυσωπῆσαι δυνάμενα, ὡς τῆς νόμος φωνῆς κειμένης ἐπὶ πλειόνων.
pass_a_gloss: To the one who said I am the life, ruling those who have borne such fruits. In that death there is not the one remembering God; for everyone who has died in it has died to God and lives to death, which is the same as living to sin. Our fruit is unto sanctification; but that which brings shame to the one already aware of it is neither ours nor according to our nature. That the better is ours, and the worse is not such, the Savior also shows saying: if you were entrusted with what is alien and were not found worthy, what will he give you that is yours? For even if we do not become worthy of the better, we do not receive it as ours by nature because of sin. Someone will say here that the fruit unto sanctification of those enslaved to God is complete purity from sexual pleasures; and such a one says that to those in marriage fits 'having been freed from sin you were enslaved to righteousness,' but to those in chastity, as something greater, 'but now having been freed from sin' and what follows; so that the one having his last fruit unto sanctification through being enslaved to God has already much earlier been enslaved to righteousness, yet does not altogether have his fruit unto sanctification because of the word about concession. Romans 6:23: for the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. Fine is the distinction: wages set upon sin, gift upon God; for God does not give wages as owed but a gift, nor does sin give a gift but owed wages. And he did not simply set the gift of God as eternal life, for that is incomplete when not in Christ Jesus our Lord. It is shown that sin gives death to the one ruled by it, and God does not bring Christ's enemy death, for God did not make death, and what follows. If someone counters with 'I will kill and make alive' and 'the Lord kills and makes alive,' we will say God kills sin so that afterward he may make alive the one who died to sin. Romans 7:1-3: or do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know law—that the law rules a human being as long as he lives? For the married woman is bound by law to the living husband; but if the husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband. So then while the husband lives she will be called an adulteress if she becomes another's; but if the husband dies she is free from the law, so as not to be an adulteress if she becomes another's. To know the law fully is to know the difference in it between the oldness of the letter and the newness of the spirit present in its meanings; for that is to know the law perfectly. He also adds an example very fitting to the matter: the married woman is bound by law to the living husband; if the husband dies she is released from the husband's law; the law is the husband—clearly the one according to the letter; for this one also admitted dying because it is oldness of letter; and what is growing old and aging is near disappearance. It is also said to die even when it does not live, so to speak, among those who wish to keep it and choose so. Romans 7:6: but now we have been released from the law, having died in that by which we were held, so that we serve in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter. The Holy Spirit is always in newness, neither growing old nor aging, but rather as our inner human is renewed day by day; and the oldness of the letter was never new, nor was our old human ever new—he who at once upon existing has grown old, not by time but by such thoughts and deeds aging him. Romans 7:7: What then? Is the law sin? Just as 'law' is one name, so there is not one account of law everywhere in Scripture. Therefore at each place one must carefully attend and observe what the word 'law' signifies now, and what one should understand by such. And likewise about many other things; for there are also homonyms elsewhere in Scripture that confound those who think that as the name is one so the meaning is one wherever it is named. That the word 'law' is set not upon the same but upon several things—leaving aside many that need construction and have a counter needing solution—we will set out what can put anyone to shame, that the word 'law' is laid upon several things.
pass_b_english: He who said [[I am the life >> Bible:John 11:25]] rules those who have borne such fruits. In that death no one remembers God: whoever has died in it has died to God and lives to death—the same as living to sin.

Our fruit runs toward sanctification; the fruit that shames the one already aware of it is neither ours nor of our nature. That the better belongs to us and the worse does not, the Savior shows: if you were entrusted with what is alien and proved unworthy, what of your own will he give you? Even when we fail to become worthy of the better, sin keeps us from receiving it as ours by nature.

Some say the sanctifying fruit of those enslaved to God is complete purity from sexual pleasure. On that reading, [[having been freed from sin you became slaves of righteousness >> Bible:Romans 6:18]] fits those in marriage, while the stronger word [[but now that you have been freed from sin >> Bible:Romans 6:22]] fits those in chastity. So the person whose final fruit is sanctification through slavery to God was already enslaved to righteousness earlier, yet may still lack that sanctifying fruit because of the word spoken by way of concession.

[[For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord >> Bible:Romans 6:23]]. The contrast is deliberate: wages for sin, gift for God. God does not pay wages as a debt; he gives a gift. Sin does not give a gift; it pays what is owed. Nor does he simply call the gift 'eternal life,' for that life is incomplete when it is not in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Sin deals death to the one it rules; God does not bring Christ's enemy, death—[[God did not make death >> Bible:Wisdom 1:13]]. If someone answers with [[I kill and I make alive >> Bible:Deuteronomy 32:39]] and [[the Lord kills and makes alive >> Bible:1 Samuel 2:6]], we say God kills sin so that afterward he may make alive the one who has died to sin.

[[Or do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know the law—that the law rules a person as long as he lives? For a married woman is bound by law to her living husband; but if the husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband. So while the husband lives she will be called an adulteress if she belongs to another; but if the husband dies she is free from the law and is not an adulteress if she belongs to another >> Bible:Romans 7:1-3]].

To know the law fully is to know the difference inside it between the oldness of the letter and the newness of the spirit in its meanings. That is perfect knowledge of the law. His example fits tightly: the married woman is bound to the living husband; if he dies she is released. The husband is the law—clearly the letter-law—which can die because it is the oldness of the letter; what grows old and ages nears disappearance. It is even said to die when it no longer truly lives among those who still claim to keep it.

[[But now we have been released from the law, having died to that which held us, so that we serve in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter >> Bible:Romans 7:6]]. The Holy Spirit is always new—neither aging nor wearing out—while our inner self is renewed day by day. The oldness of the letter was never new, and our old self was never young: it aged at once, not by the clock but by the thoughts and deeds that made it old.

[[What then? Is the law sin? >> Bible:Romans 7:7]] 'Law' is one word, but Scripture does not mean one thing by it everywhere. At each place you must ask what 'law' signifies now. The same holds for many other shared names in Scripture that confuse readers who think one sound means one sense wherever it appears. Leaving aside harder cases that need construction and replies, it is enough to shame anyone into admitting that 'law' is laid on several realities.

choices.choice: Kept Origen's sharp wage/gift contrast: sin pays debt; God gives grace.
Identified the dying husband with the letter-law, matching Origen's example.
